message.content:
In Christian theology, the focus is generally on the life, teachings, death, and resurrection of Jesus Christ as the central narrative of salvation history. Jesus is often described as the fulfillment of Old‑Testament prophetic expectations, and many Christians regard Him as the ultimate revelation of God’s will.

At the same time, the Old Testament prophets—such as Moses, Isaiah, Jeremiah, and others—are highly respected for their role in shaping Israel’s covenantal relationship with God and for foreshadowing the coming of the Messiah. Different Christian traditions may emphasize particular prophets or highlight certain prophetic books for theological study, liturgical readings, or moral instruction.

So while Jesus is typically seen as the pivotal figure in Christian faith, the prophets of the Hebrew Scriptures are also regarded as foundational teachers and messengers whose writings continue to inform Christian doctrine, worship, and ethics.
